clue.text: People talking too much, holding up balloons?

definitions.meaning: windbags, chatterers who never stop talking
the gas-filled envelopes that keep a balloon or airship aloft

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a windbag talker, and the gas-filled bags inside balloons and airships that provide lift.

clue.text: The great film of the book!

definitions.text: The great film of the book!

parts.words: The great film of the book!
parts.note: a cryptic nod to an F. Scott Fitzgerald novel whose title begins 'The Great', later filmed; the missing title word is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'The great' is not praise: it is the start of the novel's title, and the answer is the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby was made into films, so its title hero completes the phrase.

clue.text: Sarah takes the Roman road to find this plant

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of Sarah
via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: Sarah walks a Roman road in search of a particular plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvia is a genus of flowering plants, the sages, grown in gardens.

clue.text: Old stringed instrument for old warden fellow — 1 (one)

parts.note: ARP stands for Air Raid Precautions, the wartime wardens in Britain
egg is old slang for a chap, as in 'good egg'
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to cross-refer to another answer while describing an old instrument for a warden.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a cross-reference to 1 across, but it is simply the numeral, giving I; the bracketed '(one)' then supplies ONE. ARP wardens patrolled British streets in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The arpeggione was a bowed, fretted six-string instrument of the 1820s, remembered through Schubert's sonata for it.

clue.text: Street song goes up and down

definitions.note: a noun answer for a verb phrase: a staircase step is what one climbs and descends on

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A tune from the street rises and falls in pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A step in a flight is the thing people climb and descend, so it cryptically carries traffic both ways.

clue.text: "Cara mia" translated into another language

indicators.note: translating changes words into a new form, so the letters of the Italian phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian endearment is rendered into a different tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' turns the letters of CARA MIA into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue, said to be the one Jesus spoke.

clue.text: Kind person with food, which is made without egg yolks

definitions.text: which is made without egg yolks

parts.note: a kind, helpful person is called an angel
cake is an item of food

explanation.surface: A generous soul brings something to eat that is baked using only egg whites.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel food cake is a light sponge made with whipped egg whites and no yolks at all.

clue.text: A book, nearly a subject

indicators.note: nearly means stopping short of the end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a book is a read, as in 'a good read'

explanation.surface: A book that almost covers a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' signals that the synonym for book loses its final letter; 'book' here is a noun for something one reads, not the verb to reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a field of study or topic, as in a subject area.

clue.text: Hit man spotted in one steamship, then another and finally at home

parts.note: a means one
a second 'one', so another A
a second steamship, so another SS
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A contract killer was seen aboard one steamship, then a second, and at last back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second copy of the whole phrase 'one steamship', and 'finally' just places the home piece at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired killer, which is what a hit man is.

clue.text: Gestures of respect nearly struck up to cover agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction is read from bottom to top
covering something means wrapping round it, so the shortened word goes around the other piece
nearly means the word stops just short, so its final letter goes

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Bows of deference, almost struck up, to hide a nod of assent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' shortens the first word, 'to cover' wraps it round the agreement, and 'up' reverses the whole thing, so the agreement word ends up backwards too, as the blog points out.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is a bob or bow of the knees made as a mark of respect, so plural curtsies are such gestures.

clue.text: Flower makes a half turn on opening

indicators.note: half the word means its first two of four letters only

parts.note: a lip is the rim of an opening, as of a jug or wound

explanation.surface: A bloom turns partly toward the light as it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TU from TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a common spring flower grown from a bulb.

clue.text: He starts a fight, spattering grass with gore

indicators.note: spattering scatters things about, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A brawler begins a scrap, splashing the lawn with blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spattering' mixes GRASS and GORE together into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is the party who attacks first or starts hostilities.

clue.text: Game to go round for some bread?

parts.note: bridge is a card game
to roll is to turn over and over or go round

explanation.surface: A game played going around the table, for a sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' looks like slang for money, but it is the baked kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge roll is a small, soft, finger-shaped bread roll.

clue.text: Habitually employs buses that fail to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone regularly takes buses that will not start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that fail to start' drops the B from BUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses a thing employs it, and a habit is regular use.

clue.text: Shutting one's eyes to hide genetic information, which is an offence

indicators.note: hiding something means putting it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: kipping is British slang for sleeping
DNA carries genetic information

explanation.surface: Dozing off to conceal one's genes is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hide' signals the container; to kip is British slang for to sleep, so the eyes are shut in sleep, not in disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapping, abducting a person, is a serious crime.

clue.text: Capriciousness in a good man with flair

parts.note: taken as written
St, for saint, is a crossword's good man
flair is talent or ability

explanation.surface: Fickleness found in a virtuous, talented person.
explanation.definitionFit: Instability means unsteadiness or changeability, much as capriciousness is unpredictable change of mood.

clue.text: Native American VIPs — wise men touring Italy's own capital

annotationWithheld.why: Native American VIPs — wise men touring Italy's own capital (9): SAGES around ROMA reversed; 'touring' must be both the container and the reversal indicator, a word doing two jobs (the blog notes no reversal indicator).

clue.text: Breakfasters need this to get grime removed

indicators.note: re-moved, moved again, so the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: People eating breakfast must have this to get the dirt off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved, rearranging GET GRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass or timer is used to boil an egg for breakfast to the right softness.

clue.text: Brave female refusing to listen?

parts.note: a playful sense of earless, lacking ears and so not hearing

explanation.surface: A courageous woman who will not hear any advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless means without fear, which is what being brave amounts to.

clue.text: King George sits atop a volcano with grass — a popular marriage spot once

indicators.note: sitting atop puts this piece first, in front of the next

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George
Etna is the volcano in Sicily
a green is a grassy area

explanation.surface: A monarch perched on a grassy volcano picks a favourite place for weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: GRETNA GREEN is the Scottish border village where eloping English couples once married under Scotland's laxer law.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretna Green was famous as the place runaway couples went to wed quickly.

clue.text: Sister of Moses says: "I'm following border the wrong way"

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the border piece in the answer
going the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge
I'm in full is I am

explanation.surface: Moses's sister declares she follows the edge back the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses the border word, and 'following' sends I'm, written in full, to the end; 'says' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Miriam is the sister of Moses and Aaron.

clue.text: Make a mark around the end of the day, but don't go out!

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to stain is to make a mark on

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Leave a mark at day's end, but stay home!
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes Y from DAY and 'around' puts STAIN round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in is to remain at home rather than going out.

clue.text: Sweet for sailor given time

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A dessert for a sailor once enough time has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry dessert, and sweet is British for pudding.

clue.text: Plumpness? Point to retiring aristocrat and me

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: a nob is a toff, an upper-class person
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion of chubbiness: point it out to a shy nobleman and me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns 'aristocrat and me' backwards as one run, and that reversed run comes before the point; nob is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Embonpoint is a French-derived term for plumpness or a well-fed figure.

clue.text: Sexiness needs two loves on speed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two of them
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: Sex appeal requires two romances and some pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for sex appeal or vigour.

clue.text: Man or woman, who loved some of the smells

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a run inside the words

explanation.surface: A person who adored part of the odours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' marks the run inside 'the smells'. The name derives from Old French for loved or esteemed.
explanation.definitionFit: Esme is a given name for either sex, derived from French esmé, meaning esteemed or beloved.

clue.text: Confusion caused by disturbance to slammer

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Chaos follows a riot in the prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' jumbles TO SLAMMER; 'slammer' is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a whirlpool, and figuratively a state of turmoil or confusion.

clue.text: Island not initially found to act in an unfriendly way

indicators.note: without its initial letter, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: Sicily is the Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: An island is not at first thought to behave coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the S from SICILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Icily means coldly, in a frosty, hostile manner.

clue.text: Plans require fowl to drop an egg

indicators.note: dropping something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: roosters are cockerels, domestic fowl
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: Schemes demand that the hens lay an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' removes one O, the egg shape, from ROOSTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster is a rota or schedule, a plan of who does what when.

clue.text: Loaded dice for Dick Turpin & Co having lost their way

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken out of the word

parts.note: Dick Turpin was a notorious 18th-century English highwayman, so he and his kind are highwaymen
way is taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheats' dice for a gang of robbers who have got lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' removes WAY from HIGHWAYMEN; Dick Turpin was a famous English highway robber.
explanation.definitionFit: High men were old slang for dice loaded to roll high numbers.
